setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line
Caution (Do Not Stop on the Tracks)

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (7 reviews): Dark Star running through into Caution is singled out as exceptional; The Dark Star is described as monstrous, and the band sounds like they enjoy Caution [5][6][7][8][9][11][13]
- **Caution (Do Not Stop on the Tracks)** (2 reviews): Pigpen delivers wild ad libs during Caution, with Jerry accompanying; the piece comes straight out of Sugar Magnolia; Reviewer says this was the last Caution and Who Do You Love, with Pigpen's health failing yet performing brilliantly [5][10]
- **Black Throated Wind** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Black Throated Wind as great, along with Morning Dew and Good Lovin' [11]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): The first-set Good Lovin' has a mellow groove that Pigpen handles flawlessly [6]
- **Who Do You Love?** (1 review): The Caution into Who Do You Love is extra hot and was Pigpen's last performance of it [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Two Souls In Communion**: rare: 10 archived performances [16]
- **Drums/Phil Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- **Who Do You Love?**: rare: 5 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd72-05-11.sbd.ashley-bertha.7364.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 34 songs; 218 min; rated 4.98/5 by 48 [1]
- **gd72-05-11.sbd.samaritano.9357.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 29 songs; 223 min; rated 4.44/5 by 34 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the sound is good [13]
- **gd1972-05-11.sbd.giles.3830.shnf**: soundboard; 30 songs; 219 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]

## Around the show

- The Rider fadeout is due to a reel flip, and the encore is missing on both sources [3]
- Reviewer places this show near the top among 1972 shows [6]
- Apart from the Dark Star, the reviewer finds it a standard 1972 gig with good setlist [13]
- Reviewer says it slips under the radar of great 1972 shows, yet ranks among the year's top five [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-05-11.sbd.ashley-bertha.7364.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBD>>MR>>DAT>>CDA>>SHN>>DAW(Bertha)>>SHN [1]. Also: Jay Ashley (Bertha) remaster from a Master Reel source [1]
- **gd72-05-11.sbd.samaritano.9357.sbeok.shnf**: source: 10" MR@7.5ips->DAT>CDR [2]
- **gd1972-05-11.sbd.giles.3830.shnf**: transferred by Bill Giles; source: Discs 1 and 2 - SBD>MR>C>DAT>CDR>EAC>SHN Discs 3 and 4 - SBD>MR>??>FM>??>CDR>editing>CDR>EAC>SHN [3]. Also: Bill Giles notes the Uncle John's Band sequence of 88 minutes opens Truckin', less abrupt than the Storch master [3]
- The show was officially released in 2011 on Grateful Dead Records as a 4 CD set in Europe '72 series [21]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead of the Day: [Dead of the Day: May 11, 1972](https://gratefuldeadoftheday.com/05-11-1972/) [22]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 5/11/72 Grote Zaal - De Doelen, Rotterdam,… | Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26826835196/) [23]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26826835196/) [24]
